author: Anthony Wood
title: Dale Earnhardt Jr. makes bold Connor Zilisch prediction ahead of NASCAR Cup Series move - NewsBreak
text:
By Anthony Wood ,
2 hours ago
Connor Zilisch's first full-time NASCAR Xfinity Series season may not yet be over, but the 19-year-old has already secured himself a move to the Cup Series in 2026 with Trackhouse Racing .
Set to replace Daniel Suarez in the No. 99 Chevrolet, Zilisch will partner with Shane van Gisbergen , whom he has already raced alongside on a handful of occasions at JR Motorsports in the Xfinity Series.
Like Zilisch, 36-year-old Supercars legend van Gisbergen is a newcomer to the Cup Series, having only joined full-time this season after one year in the Xfinity Series. However, according to JR Motorsports owner Dale Earnhardt Jr. , the New Zealander's presence could prove hugely beneficial to the youngster, with the NASCAR Hall of Famer predicting big things for Zilisch in 2026.
Following Zilisch's record-breaking ninth win of the season at the wheel of the No. 87 JRM Chevrolet, and his seventh win in the last eight races, Earnhardt previewed what he expects from the Red Bull-sponsored athlete once he makes the leap to the Cup.
The 50-year-old suggested, on his ' Dale Jr. Download ' podcast, that Zilisch may well "be mid-pack a lot," partially due to Trackhouse's "hot and cold vibe," and partially because of how much adjusting he will have to make, taking to the wheel of the NextGen car.

Zilisch and Shane van Gisbergen have already been teammates at JR Motorsports However, Earnhardt also expects that after a year in the Cup Series, van Gisbergen will be well equipped to help Zilisch learn the ropes, commenting, "Connor's going to benefit from all of that knowledge coming in straightaway.
"And then he'll have his own ability plus a reasonably solid race car, and then Connor then too can start to improve on the car."
Earnhardt went on to predict that Zilisch, well-known for his ability on road courses, could battle "for a win on a road course" in 2026. Although when it comes to ovals, his expectations are more tempered.

"Everywhere else, he's learning an entirely new car. The short sidewall, the way this car feels, the way the car reacts and steps out, and all of those things will be very unique and different than what he's experienced in the Xfinity car," Earnhardt said.
"So he's got to build up this sort of data point or build up an entirely new notebook internally about what the car is capable of doing and how to push the car."
Such a season would be far from unusual for Trackhouse, all but mirroring that of van Gisbergen.
The three-time Supercars Championship winner, who won in his Cup Series debut in 2023, has made it to victory lane on four occasions this season - all of which were at road courses. As for ovals, he has yet to crack the top 10, reaching a high of 14th at both Richmond Raceway and Charlotte Motor Speedway.
However, as mentioned by Earnhardt, van Gisbergen believes he is turning a corner when it comes to ovals . "We're still a long way from winning a race or being complete, but I can feel and see where the time is," he told Earnhardt in August.
"I'm having more moments where I have a couple of good sections of a race or feel the car doing something, and I'm, 'Oh, there it is. There's the limit.' And I'm getting closer to that every week. And I'm feeling it more often."
But in the meantime, Zilisch's focus will remain on making the most of the opportunities he has left to impress in the Xfinity Series. On Friday, he will kickstart his first Playoff campaign in the Round of 12 at Bristol Motor Speedway, before heading to Kansas Speedway the following week.
